To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the photovoltaics industry is growing in proportion to its size, and (2) this proportionality is determined by the capacity-normalized capital investment and demand rates.

(a) the photovoltaics industry will grow if the annual global investment rate in photovoltaic manufacturing capacity (CapIR) is greater than 0.5 $/W and (b) the photovoltaic industry will grow faster if the capital demand rate (CapDR) is less than 1.0 $/W.

(1) the global investment in manufacturing for photovoltaic solar modules tends to grow at the rate of CapIR times the manufacturing capacity, (2) CapIR is the annual investment in manufacturing normalized to the manufacturing, and (3) the capital investment per watt of manufacturing capacity normalized to its service life, CapDR, is a good proxy for the cost of manufacturing.
